source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֧וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And did [the] sons of Israel the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and gave them Yahweh into [the] hand of Midian seven years.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them into [the] hand of Midian seven years.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them into the power of Midian for seven years.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed them over to the Midianites for seven years.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakafanya maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mkononi mwa Midiani miaka saba.
sw.B: Waisraeli walifanya maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mikononi mwa Midiani kwa miaka saba.
sw.R: Waisraeli walifanya yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema ni maovu. Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia mikononi mwa Wamidiani kwa miaka saba.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel hicieron lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó en mano de Madián siete años.
es.B: Los israelitas hicieron lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó en poder de Madián durante siete años.
es.R: Los israelitas hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que era malo. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó a los madianitas durante siete años.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël firent le mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les livra dans la main de Madian sept ans.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent ce qui est mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les livra au pouvoir de Madian pendant sept ans.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déclarait mauvais. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a livrés aux Madianites pendant sept ans.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phó họ vào tay Ma-đi-an bảy năm.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giao họ vào tay Ma-đi-an trong bảy năm.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho là ác. Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giao họ cho người Ma-đi-an trong bảy năm.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈에 악한 일을 했다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 칠 년 동안 미디안의 손에 주셨다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 보시기에 악한 일을 했다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들을 칠 년 동안 미디안의 손에 넘기셨다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 악하다고 하신 일을 했다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 칠 년 동안 그들을 미디안 사람들에게 넘기셨다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel fizeram o mal aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os entregou na mão de Midiã sete anos.
pt.B: Os israelitas fizeram o que era mau aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os entregou ao poder de Midiã por sete anos.
pt.R: Os israelitas fizeram o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} considerava mau. Por isso {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os entregou aos midianitas por sete anos.

decisions.choice: the pattern of Judges begins again: Israel does evil, and Yahweh hands them over
decisions.reason: This is the fourth turn of the cycle described in 2:11-19 (3:7-8, 12; 4:1-2). After the forty years of peace that followed Deborah's victory (5:31), Israel again turns away, and Yahweh gives them into the power of an enemy.

decisions.choice: gave them into the hand of Midian: put them under Midian's power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and control. Yahweh lets Midian overpower Israel; the same picture returns in verses 2, 9, 13 and 14.

decisions.choice: Midian: a people of the desert regions east and south of Israel
decisions.reason: The Midianites were traced back to Abraham through Keturah (Genesis 25:1-2). They lived as herders and traders, and they had joined Moab against Israel in the wilderness (Numbers 22:4; 25:6-18; 31:1-12).

decisions.choice: gave them into the power of (Balanced); handed them over to (Readable)
decisions.reason: As with "sold them into the hand of" elsewhere in Judges, Balanced turns "hand" into "power" and Readable says "handed them over". Readable names the people, "the Midianites", for the nation "Midian".

decisions.choice: "Madián", "los madianitas"; in this chapter also "Ofra", "Joás el abiezerita", "Gedeón", "Jerobaal", "el valle de Jezreel", "Abiezer", "Aser", "Zabulón", "Neftalí"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges: names follow the usual Spanish forms, as the terms note for these books sets ("Gedeón", "Jerobaal", "los madianitas"). "Gedeón" is also the form of Hebrews 11:32 in this translation.

decisions.choice: the names of chapters 6-8: "Ma-đi-an", "Óp-ra", "Giô-ách", "A-bi-ê-xe", "Ghê-đê-ôn", "Giê-ru-ba-anh", "Gít-rê-ên"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms, as the terms note sets; "Ghê-đê-ôn" is the form of the Vietnamese Hebrews 11:32.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B, R); no gender setting
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch and Joshua in Portuguese (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md): "filhos" already includes daughters and "os israelitas" is the plain name, so there is nothing for the English gender setting to change, here and through Gideon's story. Readable names "os midianitas" for the nation "Midiã", as the English does.

source.text: וַתָּ֥עָז יַד־מִדְיָ֖ן עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִפְּנֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן עָשֽׂוּ לָהֶ֣ם׀בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶת־הַמִּנְהָרוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וְאֶת־הַמְּעָר֖וֹת וְאֶת־הַמְּצָדֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And prevailed [the] hand of Midian over Israel; because of Midian made for themselves [the] sons of Israel the dens which [are] in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.

en.L: And the hand of Midian prevailed over Israel. Because of Midian the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel made for themselves the dens that [are] in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.
en.B: Midian's power weighed heavily on Israel. Because of Midian, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} made themselves the hiding places in the mountains, and the caves and the strongholds.
en.R: The Midianites had so much power over Israel that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} made hiding places for themselves in the hills. They also used caves and places that were hard to reach.

sw.L: Na mkono wa Midiani ukawa na nguvu juu ya Israeli. Kwa sababu ya Midiani wana wa Israeli wakajifanyia mapango [yaliyo] milimani, na pango, na ngome.
sw.B: Nguvu za Midiani ziliwalemea sana Israeli. Kwa sababu ya Midiani, Waisraeli walijitengenezea maficho milimani, na mapango, na ngome.
sw.R: Wamidiani walikuwa na nguvu nyingi juu ya Israeli, hata Waisraeli wakajitengenezea mahali pa kujificha milimani. Pia walitumia mapango na mahali pasipofikika kwa urahisi.

es.L: Y la mano de Madián prevaleció sobre Israel. Por causa de Madián los hijos de Israel se hicieron las cuevas que [hay] en los montes, y las cavernas, y las fortalezas.
es.B: El poder de Madián pesaba sobre Israel. Por causa de Madián, los israelitas se hicieron los escondites que hay en los montes, y las cavernas y las fortalezas.
es.R: Los madianitas tenían tanto poder sobre Israel que los israelitas se hicieron escondites en las colinas. También usaban cuevas y lugares difíciles de alcanzar.

fr.L: Et la main de Madian l’emporta sur Israël. À cause de Madian, les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël se firent les repaires qui [sont] dans les montagnes, et les cavernes, et les forteresses.
fr.B: La puissance de Madian pesa lourdement sur Israël. À cause de Madian, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se firent les abris qu’on voit dans les montagnes, les cavernes et les forteresses.
fr.R: Les Madianites avaient tellement de pouvoir sur Israël que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se sont fait des cachettes dans les collines. Ils se sont aussi servis de grottes et d’endroits difficiles à atteindre.

vi.L: Và tay của Ma-đi-an mạnh hơn Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vì Ma-đi-an, con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên làm cho mình những hang hốc trên núi, và các hang động, và các đồn lũy.
vi.B: Quyền lực của Ma-đi-an đè nặng trên Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vì Ma-đi-an, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên phải làm cho mình những nơi ẩn núp trên núi, cùng các hang động và đồn lũy.
vi.R: Người Ma-đi-an có quyền lực trên Y-sơ-ra-ên đến nỗi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên phải làm những chỗ ẩn núp cho mình trên đồi núi. Họ cũng dùng các hang động và những nơi khó đến được.

ko.L: 그리고 미디안의 손이 이스라엘을 이겼다. 미디안 때문에 이스라엘 자손이 산에 있는 굴들과 동굴들과 요새들을 자기들을 위하여 만들었다.
ko.B: 미디안의 세력이 이스라엘을 무겁게 짓눌렀다. 미디안 때문에 이스라엘 백성은 산에 숨을 곳을 만들고, 동굴과 요새를 마련했다.
ko.R: 미디안 사람들의 힘이 너무 강해서, 이스라엘 백성은 산속에 숨을 곳을 만들었다. 동굴과 사람이 오르기 어려운 곳에도 숨었다.

pt.L: E a mão de Midiã prevaleceu sobre Israel. Por causa de Midiã, os filhos de Israel fizeram para si as covas que [estão] nos montes, e as cavernas, e as fortalezas.
pt.B: O poder de Midiã pesou muito sobre Israel. Por causa de Midiã, os israelitas fizeram para si os esconderijos nos montes, as cavernas e as fortalezas.
pt.R: Os midianitas tinham tanto poder sobre Israel que os israelitas fizeram esconderijos para si nas montanhas. Eles também usavam cavernas e lugares difíceis de alcançar.

decisions.choice: dens: shelters cut or dug into the hillsides, perhaps clefts in the rock
decisions.reason: The word appears only here in the Bible, so its exact sense is not certain. It comes from a word family linked with light or with channels, and may name holes or crevices in the rock that let in light, or tunnels dug as hiding places. The context makes clear that they were places to hide from the raiders.

decisions.choice: strongholds: high places that are hard to reach
decisions.reason: The word is used of rugged heights where people could hold out against attackers, as David did in the strongholds of the wilderness (1 Samuel 23:14).

decisions.choice: the dens, the caves, the strongholds: places the first readers knew
decisions.reason: Each noun has the article, as if the writer is pointing to hiding places that were still known in the hills in his own day.

decisions.choice: places that were hard to reach
decisions.reason: Readable explains "strongholds" by what made them useful: attackers could not easily get to them.

decisions.choice: as covas (L); os esconderijos (B)
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here (m1). Literal says "covas", holes dug or cut in the hillside; Balanced says what they were for, "esconderijos", as the English Balanced says "hiding places".

source.text: וְהָיָ֖ה אִם־זָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעָלָ֨ה מִדְיָ֧ן וַֽעֲמָלֵ֛ק וּבְנֵי־קֶ֖דֶם וְעָל֥וּ עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, whenever sowed Israel, then came up Midian and Amalek and [the] sons of [the] east, and they came up against him.

en.L: And it would be, whenever Israel had sown, Midian and Amalek and the {{gender:people|sons}} of the east would come up, and they would come up against them.
en.B: Whenever Israel had sown its crops, the Midianites and the Amalekites and the peoples of the east would come up and attack them.
en.R: Every time the Israelites planted their crops, the Midianites came up to attack them. The Amalekites and other people from the east came with them.

sw.L: Ikawa, kila mara Israeli walipokuwa wamepanda mbegu, Midiani na Amaleki na wana wa mashariki walipanda, nao wakapanda dhidi yao.
sw.B: Kila mara Israeli walipopanda mazao yao, Wamidiani na Waamaleki na watu wa mashariki walikuja kuwashambulia.
sw.R: Kila mara Waisraeli walipopanda mazao yao, Wamidiani walikuja kuwashambulia. Waamaleki na watu wengine kutoka mashariki walikuja pamoja nao.

es.L: Y sucedía que, cuando Israel había sembrado, subían Madián y Amalec y los hijos del oriente, y subían contra ellos.
es.B: Cada vez que Israel había sembrado sus cultivos, los madianitas, los amalecitas y los pueblos del oriente subían y los atacaban.
es.R: Cada vez que los israelitas sembraban sus cultivos, los madianitas subían a atacarlos. Los amalecitas y otros pueblos del oriente venían con ellos.

fr.L: Et il arrivait, chaque fois qu’Israël avait semé, que Madian et Amalek et les {{gender:gens|fils}} de l’Orient montaient, et ils montaient contre eux.
fr.B: Chaque fois qu’Israël avait fait ses semailles, les Madianites, les Amalécites et les peuples de l’Orient montaient l’attaquer.
fr.R: Chaque fois que les Israélites semaient leurs champs, les Madianites venaient les attaquer. Les Amalécites et d’autres peuples de l’Orient venaient avec eux.

vi.L: Và hễ khi Y-sơ-ra-ên gieo giống, thì Ma-đi-an và A-ma-léc và con cái phương Đông kéo lên, và họ kéo lên đánh dân ấy.
vi.B: Mỗi khi Y-sơ-ra-ên gieo trồng, người Ma-đi-an, người A-ma-léc và các dân phương Đông lại kéo lên tấn công họ.
vi.R: Mỗi lần dân Y-sơ-ra-ên gieo trồng, người Ma-đi-an lại kéo lên tấn công họ. Người A-ma-léc và những dân khác từ phương Đông cũng đi theo.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘이 씨를 뿌리면, 미디안과 아말렉과 동방 사람들이 올라오곤 하였다. 그들이 그들을 치러 올라오곤 하였다.
ko.B: 이스라엘이 씨를 뿌려 놓으면, 미디안 사람들과 아말렉 사람들과 동방 사람들이 올라와서 그들을 공격하곤 했다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들이 곡식을 심을 때마다 미디안 사람들이 쳐들어왔다. 아말렉 사람들과 동쪽에서 온 다른 사람들도 함께 왔다.

pt.L: E acontecia que, sempre que Israel semeava, Midiã e Amaleque e os povos do oriente subiam, e subiam contra eles.
pt.B: Sempre que Israel semeava, os midianitas, os amalequitas e os povos do oriente subiam e o atacavam.
pt.R: Toda vez que os israelitas plantavam, os midianitas subiam para atacá-los. Os amalequitas e outros povos do oriente vinham com eles.

decisions.choice: would come up: something that happened again and again
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe a repeated pattern, not a single raid. Every year, after Israel had sown, the raiders came back at harvest time to take the crops.

decisions.choice: Amalek and the people of the east: other desert peoples who joined Midian
decisions.reason: Amalek was Israel's old enemy from the wilderness (Exodus 17:8-16; 3:13 in this book). "The people of the east" is a broad name for the tribes of the desert east of the Jordan (Genesis 29:1; Job 1:3).

decisions.choice: against him: against Israel as one people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "against him", treating Israel as a single person, as in the first half of the verse ("Israel sowed").

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: English uses "them" for the nation, since "him" would sound like one man.

decisions.choice: the imparfait for what the raiders did year after year (verses 3-5) at every level
alternatives: the passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes something that happened again and again, every year at sowing time, as the meaning decision says. French marks repeated actions in the past with the imparfait at every level, Readable included.

decisions.choice: acontecia, semeava, subiam (imperfect); os povos do oriente, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The raids came back year after year (m1), so Portuguese narrates them in the imperfect, the tense for what used to happen, through verse 5. "Os povos do oriente" is the form Genesis 29:1 has in Portuguese; it already means the peoples, so there is no gender setting for the English "people / sons". Literal says "contra eles" for the Hebrew "against him", as the English says "them" (r-en-1); Balanced can keep the singular "o atacavam", since its subject "Israel" is singular in Portuguese too.

source.text: וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשְׁחִ֨יתוּ֙ אֶת־יְב֣וּל הָאָ֔רֶץ עַד־בּוֹאֲךָ֖ עַזָּ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁאִ֤ירוּ מִֽחְיָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֶׂ֥ה וָשׁ֖וֹר וַחֲמֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they camped against them and destroyed [the] produce of the land as far as your coming to Gaza, and not they left sustenance in Israel, and sheep and ox and donkey.

en.L: And they camped against them and destroyed the produce of the land as far as your coming to Gaza, and they did not leave sustenance in Israel, or sheep or ox or donkey.
en.B: They would camp on their land and ruin the crops all the way to Gaza. They left nothing in Israel to live on, not a sheep, an ox or a donkey.
en.R: They set up camp on the Israelites' land and ruined the crops as far as the city of Gaza. They left the Israelites nothing to eat, and no sheep, cattle or donkeys.

sw.L: Nao wakapiga kambi dhidi yao, wakaharibu mazao ya nchi mpaka kufika kwako Gaza, wala hawakuacha chakula katika Israeli, wala kondoo, wala ng'ombe, wala punda.
sw.B: Walipiga kambi katika nchi yao na kuharibu mazao mpaka Gaza. Hawakuacha chochote katika Israeli cha kuwalisha, wala kondoo, wala ng'ombe, wala punda.
sw.R: Walipiga kambi katika nchi ya Waisraeli na kuharibu mazao mpaka mji wa Gaza. Hawakuwaachia Waisraeli chakula chochote, wala kondoo, ng'ombe au punda.

es.L: Y acampaban contra ellos y destruían el fruto de la tierra hasta llegar a Gaza, y no dejaban sustento en Israel, ni oveja, ni buey, ni asno.
es.B: Acampaban en su tierra y arruinaban las cosechas hasta Gaza. No dejaban en Israel nada con qué vivir, ni una oveja, ni un buey, ni un asno.
es.R: Ponían su campamento en la tierra de los israelitas y arruinaban las cosechas hasta la ciudad de Gaza. No les dejaban a los israelitas nada que comer, ni ovejas, ni ganado, ni burros.

fr.L: Et ils campaient contre eux et détruisaient les produits du pays jusqu’à ton arrivée à Gaza, et ils ne laissaient pas de quoi vivre en Israël, ni mouton, ni bœuf, ni âne.
fr.B: Ils campaient sur leurs terres et ravageaient les récoltes jusqu’à Gaza. Ils ne laissaient en Israël rien pour vivre, pas un mouton, pas un bœuf, pas un âne.
fr.R: Ils installaient leur camp sur les terres des Israélites et détruisaient les récoltes jusqu’à la ville de Gaza. Ils ne laissaient aux Israélites rien à manger, ni moutons, ni bœufs, ni ânes.

vi.L: Và họ đóng trại đối diện dân ấy, và phá hủy hoa màu của đất cho đến tận lối vào Ga-xa, và không để lại thức ăn gì trong Y-sơ-ra-ên, cả chiên, bò hay lừa cũng không.
vi.B: Họ đóng trại trên đất của dân ấy và phá hủy mùa màng cho đến tận Ga-xa. Họ không để lại gì cho Y-sơ-ra-ên để sống, không một con chiên, con bò hay con lừa nào.
vi.R: Họ đóng trại trên đất của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và phá hủy mùa màng cho đến tận thành Ga-xa. Họ không để lại cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên thứ gì để ăn, cũng không để lại chiên, bò hay lừa.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그들을 향하여 진을 치고, 가사에 이르기까지 그 땅의 소산을 망쳐 놓았다. 그리고 이스라엘에 먹을 것을 남겨 두지 않았고, 양도 소도 나귀도 [남겨 두지 않았다].
ko.B: 그들은 이스라엘 땅에 진을 치고 가사에 이르기까지 농작물을 망쳐 놓았다. 그들은 이스라엘에 먹고살 것을 하나도 남기지 않았고, 양도 소도 나귀도 남기지 않았다.
ko.R: 그들은 이스라엘 사람들의 땅에 진을 치고, 가사 성까지 곡식을 다 망쳐 놓았다. 그들은 이스라엘 사람들에게 먹을 것을 하나도 남기지 않았고, 양도 소도 나귀도 남기지 않았다.

pt.L: E acampavam contra eles e destruíam a produção da terra até a tua chegada a Gaza, e não deixavam sustento em Israel, nem ovelha, nem boi, nem jumento.
pt.B: Eles acampavam na terra de Israel e arruinavam as colheitas até Gaza. Não deixavam em Israel nada de que viver, nem ovelha, nem boi, nem jumento.
pt.R: Eles acampavam na terra dos israelitas e destruíam as plantações até a cidade de Gaza. Não deixavam para os israelitas nada para comer, nem ovelhas, nem bois, nem jumentos.

decisions.choice: as far as your coming to Gaza: all the way to Gaza
decisions.reason: "As you come to" is a common way of giving a distance (Genesis 10:19). Gaza was on the coast in the far southwest, so the raiders swept across the whole land from the Jordan to the sea.

decisions.choice: sustenance: food, what keeps people alive
decisions.reason: The word means the means of life. The raiders took or ruined the grain and drove off the animals, leaving people with nothing to live on (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the city of Gaza
decisions.reason: Readable says that Gaza was a city for readers who do not know the name.

source.text: כִּ֡י הֵם֩ וּמִקְנֵיהֶ֨ם יַעֲל֜וּ וְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם וּבָ֤אוּ כְדֵֽי־אַרְבֶּה֙ לָרֹ֔ב וְלָהֶ֥ם וְלִגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For they and their livestock would come up, and their tents, and they would come like [the] abundance of locust[s] for multitude; and to them and to their camels there was no number, and they came into the land to destroy it.

en.L: For they and their livestock would come up, and their tents, and they would come like a swarm of locusts for multitude; and of them and of their camels there was no number; and they came into the land to destroy it.
en.B: They came up with their livestock and their tents, as thick as a swarm of locusts. There was no counting them or their camels, and they came into the land to lay it waste.
en.R: They brought their animals and their tents with them. There were so many of them that they were like swarms of locusts. No one could count all the people and their camels. They came into the land to destroy it.

sw.L: Kwa maana wao na mifugo yao walipanda, pamoja na hema zao, wakaja kama wingi wa nzige kwa wingi; wao na ngamia wao hawakuwa na hesabu; nao wakaingia nchini ili kuiharibu.
sw.B: Walikuja pamoja na mifugo yao na hema zao, wengi kama kundi la nzige. Wao na ngamia wao hawakuhesabika, nao wakaingia nchini ili kuifanya ukiwa.
sw.R: Walileta wanyama wao na hema zao. Walikuwa wengi mno, kama makundi ya nzige. Hakuna aliyeweza kuwahesabu watu hao na ngamia wao. Waliingia nchini ili kuiharibu.

es.L: Porque ellos y su ganado subían, y sus tiendas, y venían como una nube de langostas en multitud; y ellos y sus camellos no tenían número; y entraban en la tierra para destruirla.
es.B: Subían con su ganado y sus tiendas, tan numerosos como una nube de langostas. No se podía contar a ellos ni a sus camellos, y entraban en la tierra para devastarla.
es.R: Traían consigo sus animales y sus tiendas. Eran tantos que parecían nubes de langostas. Nadie podía contar a toda esa gente ni a sus camellos. Entraban en la tierra para destruirla.

fr.L: Car eux et leurs troupeaux montaient, et leurs tentes, et ils venaient comme une nuée de sauterelles en multitude ; et eux et leurs chameaux étaient sans nombre ; et ils venaient dans le pays pour le dévaster.
fr.B: Ils montaient avec leurs troupeaux et leurs tentes, aussi nombreux qu’une nuée de sauterelles. On ne pouvait les compter, ni eux ni leurs chameaux, et ils venaient dans le pays pour le ravager.
fr.R: Ils amenaient avec eux leurs bêtes et leurs tentes. Ils étaient si nombreux qu’ils ressemblaient à des nuées de sauterelles. Personne ne pouvait compter tous ces gens et leurs chameaux. Ils venaient dans le pays pour le détruire.

vi.L: Vì họ cùng súc vật và lều trại mình kéo lên, và họ đến đông như đàn châu chấu; và họ cùng lạc đà của họ thì không đếm xuể; và họ vào xứ để phá hủy nó.
vi.B: Họ kéo lên cùng với súc vật và lều trại, đông như đàn châu chấu. Không ai đếm được họ và lạc đà của họ, và họ vào xứ để tàn phá.
vi.R: Họ đem theo súc vật và lều trại của mình. Họ đông như những đàn châu chấu. Không ai đếm được hết người và lạc đà của họ. Họ vào xứ để phá hủy xứ.

ko.L: 그들과 그들의 가축이 올라왔고, 그들의 장막들도 [올라왔다]. 그들은 메뚜기 떼처럼 많이 왔다. 그들과 그들의 낙타들은 셀 수 없었다. 그리고 그들이 그 땅을 망치려고 들어왔다.
ko.B: 그들은 가축과 장막을 가지고 메뚜기 떼처럼 몰려왔다. 그들과 그들의 낙타는 셀 수조차 없었다. 그들은 그 땅을 황폐하게 하려고 들어왔다.
ko.R: 그들은 짐승들과 장막들을 가지고 왔다. 그 수가 얼마나 많은지 메뚜기 떼 같았다. 아무도 그 사람들과 낙타들을 다 셀 수 없었다. 그들은 그 땅을 망치려고 들어왔다.

pt.L: Porque eles e os seus rebanhos subiam, e as suas tendas, e vinham como um enxame de gafanhotos em multidão; e deles e dos seus camelos não havia número; e entravam na terra para destruí-la.
pt.B: Eles subiam com os seus rebanhos e as suas tendas, numerosos como um enxame de gafanhotos. Não era possível contar nem a eles nem aos seus camelos, e invadiam a terra para devastá-la.
pt.R: Eles traziam os seus animais e as suas tendas. Eram tantos que pareciam nuvens de gafanhotos. Ninguém conseguia contar todas aquelas pessoas e os seus camelos. Eles vinham à terra para destruí-la.

decisions.choice: they would come (the reading the scribes marked)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "they would come" without "and"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "and they would come". Both use the same verb, and the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: like a swarm of locusts: countless and devouring everything
decisions.reason: Locusts are a picture both of vast numbers and of total ruin, as in the plague on Egypt, when they ate every green thing (Exodus 10:4-15). The raiders strip the land the same way.

decisions.choice: camels: the raiders rode camels
decisions.reason: Camels let desert peoples cover long distances quickly and carry off what they took. A force on camels in such numbers would have been terrifying to farmers on foot.

decisions.choice: to lay it waste
decisions.reason: Balanced varies the verb "destroy", used already in verse 4, with an expression that keeps its sense: to ruin the land completely.

en.R: Israel became very poor because of the Midianites. So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help.

sw.L: Naye Israeli akadhoofika sana kwa sababu ya Midiani, nao wana wa Israeli wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

es.B: Israel quedó en gran pobreza por causa de Madián, y los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Israel se volvió muy pobre por causa de los madianitas. Así que los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda.

fr.L: Et Israël fut très affaibli à cause de Madian, et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël crièrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Israël fut réduit à une grande misère à cause de Madian, et les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} crièrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Les Madianites ont rendu Israël très pauvre. Alors les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont appelé {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au secours.

vi.L: Và Y-sơ-ra-ên bị suy kiệt lắm vì Ma-đi-an, và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Y-sơ-ra-ên bị bần cùng vì Ma-đi-an, và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Y-sơ-ra-ên trở nên rất nghèo khổ vì người Ma-đi-an. Vì vậy dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘이 미디안 때문에 몹시 약해졌다. 그래서 이스라엘 자손이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다.
ko.B: 이스라엘은 미디안 때문에 몹시 가난해졌다. 그래서 이스라엘 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다.
ko.R: 이스라엘은 미디안 사람들 때문에 아주 가난해졌다. 그래서 이스라엘 백성은 도와 달라고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다.

pt.L: E Israel foi muito empobrecido por causa de Midiã, e os filhos de Israel clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}.
pt.B: Israel ficou muito empobrecido por causa de Midiã, e os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}.
pt.R: Israel ficou muito pobre por causa dos midianitas. Então os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, pedindo ajuda.

decisions.choice: was brought low: became poor and weak
decisions.reason: The verb means to become small, thin or poor. It is related to the word Gideon uses for his clan, "the weakest" (verse 15).

decisions.choice: cried out: called for help in distress
decisions.reason: The verb is used of people crying out under oppression, the step in the pattern of Judges that comes before Yahweh sends help (3:9, 15; 4:3).

decisions.choice: for help
decisions.reason: Readable adds "for help", as at each cry in the book (3:9, 15; 4:3; 10:10), to show what kind of crying out this was.

en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help because of what the Midianites were doing to them.

fr.B: Quand les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} crièrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} à cause de Madian,

ko.B: 이스라엘 백성이 미디안 때문에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖자,
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 미디안 사람들이 자기들에게 하는 일 때문에 도와 달라고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando os filhos de Israel clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} por causa de Midiã,
pt.B: Quando os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} por causa de Midiã,
pt.R: Os israelitas clamaram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, pedindo ajuda por causa do que os midianitas estavam fazendo com eles.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 8
decisions.reason: "And it happened, when ..." sets the time for what follows: Yahweh's first answer is not a rescuer but a prophet with a rebuke (verses 8-10). Repeating the cry from verse 6 slows the story at this point.

decisions.choice: on account of Midian: because of what Midian was doing
decisions.reason: The phrase means "concerning" or "because of". Israel's cry is about Midian's raids, not yet about their own unfaithfulness, which the prophet will name.

decisions.choice: because of what the Midianites were doing to them
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "on account of Midian" means, and ends the sentence here; verse 8 begins a new one with "So".

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 자손에게 한 사람, 곧 예언자를 보내셨다. 그가 그들에게 말했다. "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. '나, 내가 너희를 이집트에서 올라오게 하였고, 종들의 집에서 너희를 이끌어 내었다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 백성에게 예언자를 한 사람 보내셨다. 그가 그들에게 말했다. "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. '너희를 이집트에서 이끌어 올린 것은 바로 나다. 내가 너희를 종살이하던 집에서 이끌어 내었다.
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 예언자를 한 사람 보내셨다. 그 예언자가 말했다. "이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. '내가 너희를 이집트에서 이끌어 냈다. 너희가 종으로 살던 땅에서 너희를 데리고 나왔다.

pt.L: {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou um homem, um profeta, aos filhos de Israel, e ele lhes disse: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: 'Eu, eu fiz vocês subirem do Egito e tirei vocês da casa de escravos.
pt.B: {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou um profeta aos israelitas, e ele lhes disse: "Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: 'Fui eu que fiz vocês subirem do Egito e tirei vocês da casa da escravidão.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou um profeta a eles. Ele disse: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, diz o seguinte: 'Eu tirei vocês do Egito. Eu tirei vocês da terra onde vocês eram escravos.

decisions.choice: a man, a prophet: a prophet whose name is not given
decisions.reason: The prophet is named only by his calling. Deborah too was a prophet (4:4). His message comes before any promise of rescue, so the people hear first why they are suffering.

decisions.choice: I, I brought you up: Yahweh and no other
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stated in addition to the verb, which puts weight on it: it was Yahweh himself who rescued Israel, not the gods they now serve (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the house of slaves: Egypt, the place of slavery
decisions.reason: The words echo the opening of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy 5:6), which go on to forbid other gods. The prophet's message follows the same order: rescue first, then the claim to sole loyalty.

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal), slavery (Balanced), where you were slaves (Readable)
decisions.reason: This is Israel's slavery in Egypt, so every level keeps the word "slave", as the style guide asks for Exodus 20:2.

decisions.choice: double quotes for the prophet, single quotes for Yahweh's words
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks, and inside his speech he quotes Yahweh. Yahweh's words take single quotes; the words Yahweh says he once spoke to Israel (verse 10) take double quotes again.

decisions.choice: "nyumba ya utumwa" (L, B) and "nchi mliyokuwa watumwa" (R): slavery in Egypt keeps the word for slavery at every level
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note keeps "mtumwa" and "utumwa" at every level for Israel's slavery in Egypt, where slavery itself is the point. Readable says what the "house" was: the land where they were slaves.

decisions.choice: « » for the prophet's words, “ ” for the LORD's words he quotes, and ‘ ’ for what the LORD had said before (verse 10)
decisions.reason: The English uses double quotation marks for the prophet and single ones for the LORD. French uses « » outside and “ ” inside, as the French style guide says, and here needs a third level for the LORD's earlier words in verse 10, for which it uses ‘ ’.

decisions.choice: "예언자" for the prophet; double quotation marks for the prophet and single ones for God's words inside, as the English
decisions.reason: "예언자" is the word this translation uses for a prophet, as the Korean style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "nhà nô lệ" (L, B); "xứ mà các ngươi làm nô lệ" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means slavery itself (m3), so the Genesis note's rule gives "nô lệ", not "đầy tớ".

decisions.choice: vocês (the LORD to Israel, verses 8-10)
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks to Israel in the plural here, so Portuguese uses "vocês" (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md). It writes "tirei vocês", "livrei vocês" rather than the object pronoun "os", because in verse 9 "os" also stands for the peoples driven out, and the two would be confused. "Da casa de escravos" (L) and "da casa da escravidão" (B) are the forms Exodus 13:3 has in Portuguese.

records.literal_gloss: And I delivered you from [the] hand of Egypt and from [the] hand of all your oppressors, and I drove them out before you and gave to you their land.

en.L: And I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all your oppressors, and I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
en.B: I rescued you from the power of Egypt and from the power of everyone who oppressed you. I drove them out ahead of you and gave you their land.
en.R: I saved you from the Egyptians and from all the others who were cruel to you. I forced them out of the land as you came in, and I gave their land to you.

sw.L: Nami nikawaokoa mkononi mwa Misri na mkononi mwa wote waliowaonea, nikawafukuza mbele yenu, nikawapa nchi yao.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:los|os}} libré de la mano de Egipto y de la mano de todos {{plural_you:sus opresores|vuestros opresores}}, y los expulsé de delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} di su tierra.
es.B: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} rescaté del poder de Egipto y del poder de todos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} oprimían. Los expulsé delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} di su tierra.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} salvé de los egipcios y de todos los demás que {{plural_you:los|os}} trataban con crueldad. Los saqué de la tierra a medida que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:entraban|entrabais}}, y {{plural_you:les|os}} di su tierra.

fr.L: Et je vous ai délivrés de la main de l’Égypte et de la main de tous vos oppresseurs, et je les ai chassés devant vous et je vous ai donné leur pays.
fr.B: Je vous ai délivrés du pouvoir de l’Égypte et du pouvoir de tous ceux qui vous opprimaient. Je les ai chassés devant vous et je vous ai donné leur pays.
fr.R: Je vous ai sauvés des Égyptiens et de tous les autres qui étaient cruels avec vous. Je les ai chassés du pays quand vous y êtes entrés, et je vous ai donné leur pays.

vi.L: Và Ta đã giải cứu các ngươi khỏi tay Ai Cập và khỏi tay mọi kẻ áp bức các ngươi, và Ta đã đuổi chúng khỏi trước mặt các ngươi và ban cho các ngươi đất của chúng.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 너희를 이집트의 손과 너희를 억압하는 모든 자의 손에서 건져 내었고, 그들을 너희 앞에서 쫓아내고 그들의 땅을 너희에게 주었다.
ko.B: 나는 너희를 이집트 사람들의 손과 너희를 억압하는 모든 자의 손에서 구해 내었다. 그들을 너희 앞에서 쫓아내고 그들의 땅을 너희에게 주었다.
ko.R: 나는 너희를 이집트 사람들에게서, 그리고 너희를 괴롭히던 다른 모든 사람에게서 구해 냈다. 너희가 들어갈 때에 나는 그들을 그 땅에서 쫓아냈고, 그들의 땅을 너희에게 주었다.

pt.L: E livrei vocês da mão do Egito e da mão de todos os seus opressores, e os expulsei de diante de vocês e dei a vocês a terra deles.
pt.B: Eu livrei vocês do poder do Egito e do poder de todos os que oprimiam vocês. Eu os expulsei de diante de vocês e dei a vocês a terra deles.
pt.R: Eu salvei vocês dos egípcios e de todos os outros que foram cruéis com vocês. Eu expulsei aqueles povos da terra enquanto vocês entravam nela, e dei a terra deles a vocês.

decisions.choice: from the hand of: from the power of
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, "hand" stands for power and control.

decisions.choice: your oppressors: those who pressed hard on you
decisions.reason: The verb means to press or squeeze. It is used of Egypt's oppression (Exodus 3:9) and of the enemies of the judges' time (2:18; 4:3).

decisions.choice: drove them out and gave you their land: the conquest under Joshua
decisions.reason: Yahweh recalls how he drove out the peoples of Canaan and gave Israel their land (Joshua 24:8-13), the same history Joshua told before the people chose to serve Yahweh alone.

decisions.choice: as you came in
decisions.reason: Readable explains "before you": the peoples were driven out as Israel entered the land.

records.literal_gloss: And I said to you, I [am] Yahweh your God; not you shall fear [the] gods of the Amorite, whom you [are] dwelling in their land. But not you listened to my voice.

en.B: I said to you, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You are not to fear the gods of the Amorites, though you live in their land." But you have not listened to me.'"
en.R: I said to you, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not worship the gods of the Amorites, even though you live in their land." But you did not obey me.'"

ko.L: 그리고 내가 너희에게 말하였다. "나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너희 하나님[이다]. 너희가 살고 있는 땅의 주인인 아모리 사람들의 신들을 두려워하지 마라." 그러나 너희는 내 목소리를 듣지 않았다.'"
ko.B: 나는 너희에게 말했다. "나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너희 하나님이다. 너희가 아모리 사람들의 땅에 살고 있더라도 그들의 신들을 두려워해서는 안 된다." 그러나 너희는 내 말을 듣지 않았다.'"
ko.R: 나는 너희에게 말했다. "나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너희 하나님이다. 너희가 아모리 사람들의 땅에 살고 있더라도 그들의 신들을 섬기지 마라." 그러나 너희는 내 말에 순종하지 않았다.'"

decisions.choice: fear: revere and worship
decisions.reason: To "fear" a god is to stand in awe of it and serve it (2 Kings 17:35-38). Israel is not to give the gods of the land the worship that belongs to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: the Amorites: the peoples of Canaan in general
decisions.reason: "Amorite" is often used as a name for all the peoples who lived in the land before Israel (Genesis 15:16; Joshua 24:15).

decisions.choice: the message ends with the charge, with no promise
decisions.reason: The prophet stops at "you have not listened". There is no word of rescue; the answer to Israel's cry comes in the next scene, when the angel of Yahweh appears to Gideon (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Do not worship
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "fear" here, to worship a god.

decisions.choice: listened to me (Balanced); obey me (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Listen to my voice" means to obey. Balanced drops "voice"; Readable says "obey".

decisions.choice: «» for the prophet's words, “ ” for the LORD's words inside them, and ‘ ’ for what the LORD had said earlier
alternatives: the same marks in another order
decisions.reason: As the Spanish style sets: quotation marks «» with “ ” inside and ‘ ’ inside those, so that the three voices of the prophet's message stay distinct, as the English uses double and single marks.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks inside single ones for the LORD's earlier words
decisions.reason: The prophet's words take double marks and the LORD's words single ones, as the English does; the LORD's own earlier saying inside them goes back to double marks, so three speakers stay apart.

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] angel of Yahweh and sat under the terebinth which [was] in Ophrah, which [belonged] to Joash the Abiezrite; and Gideon his son [was] beating out wheat in the winepress to hide [it] from before Midian.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came and sat under the terebinth that [was] in Ophrah, which [belonged] to Joash the Abiezrite; and Gideon his son [was] beating out wheat in the winepress to hide [it] from Midian.
en.B: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Ophrah and sat down under the terebinth there, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. Gideon, Joash's son, was beating out wheat in the winepress so that the Midianites would not see it.
en.R: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the town of Ophrah. He sat down under a big tree there that belonged to Joash, from the family of Abiezer. Joash's son Gideon was beating the grain out of some wheat inside a winepress. He was doing it there so that the Midianites would not find the wheat.

sw.L: Naye malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaja akaketi chini ya mwaloni [uliokuwa] huko Ofra, [uliokuwa] mali ya Yoashi Mwabiezeri; naye Gideoni mwanawe [alikuwa] akipura ngano shinikizoni, ili [kuificha] mbele ya Midiani.
sw.B: Kisha malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuja Ofra, akaketi chini ya mwaloni ulioko huko, uliokuwa mali ya Yoashi Mwabiezeri. Gideoni, mwana wa Yoashi, alikuwa akipura ngano ndani ya shinikizo la zabibu ili Wamidiani wasiione.
sw.R: Kisha malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuja katika mji wa Ofra. Aliketi chini ya mti mkubwa uliokuwa mali ya Yoashi, wa ukoo wa Abiezeri. Mwana wa Yoashi, Gideoni, alikuwa akipura ngano ndani ya shinikizo la zabibu. Alifanya hivyo huko ili Wamidiani wasiione ngano hiyo.

es.L: Y vino el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y se sentó debajo de la encina que [estaba] en Ofra, que [pertenecía] a Joás el abiezerita; y Gedeón su hijo [estaba] sacudiendo trigo en el lagar para esconder[lo] de Madián.
es.B: Entonces el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a Ofra y se sentó debajo de la encina que había allí, la cual pertenecía a Joás el abiezerita. Gedeón, hijo de Joás, estaba sacudiendo trigo en el lagar para que los madianitas no lo vieran.
es.R: Entonces el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a la ciudad de Ofra. Se sentó debajo de un árbol grande que había allí y que pertenecía a Joás, de la familia de Abiezer. Gedeón, el hijo de Joás, estaba sacudiendo unas espigas de trigo para sacarles el grano dentro de un lagar. Lo hacía allí para que los madianitas no encontraran el trigo.

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} vint et s’assit sous le térébinthe qui [était] à Ophra, qui [appartenait] à Joas l’Abiézrite ; et Gédéon, son fils, battait du blé dans le pressoir pour [le] cacher à Madian.
fr.B: Puis l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} vint à Ophra et s’assit sous le térébinthe qui s’y trouvait et qui appartenait à Joas l’Abiézrite. Gédéon, le fils de Joas, battait du blé dans le pressoir pour que les Madianites ne le voient pas.
fr.R: Puis l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est venu dans la ville d’Ophra. Il s’est assis sous un grand arbre qui appartenait à Joas, de la famille d’Abiézer. Gédéon, le fils de Joas, battait du blé pour en faire sortir le grain à l’intérieur d’un pressoir. Il faisait cela là-bas pour que les Madianites ne trouvent pas le blé.

vi.L: Và thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến và ngồi dưới cây sồi ở Óp-ra, [là cây] thuộc về Giô-ách người A-bi-ê-xe; và Ghê-đê-ôn, con trai ông, [đang] đập lúa mì trong bồn ép nho để giấu [nó] khỏi Ma-đi-an.
vi.B: Bấy giờ thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến Óp-ra và ngồi dưới cây sồi tại đó, thuộc về Giô-ách người A-bi-ê-xe. Ghê-đê-ôn, con trai Giô-ách, đang đập lúa mì trong bồn ép nho để người Ma-đi-an không thấy.
vi.R: Bấy giờ thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến thành Óp-ra. Thiên sứ ngồi dưới một cây lớn ở đó, thuộc về Giô-ách, người thuộc dòng họ A-bi-ê-xe. Ghê-đê-ôn, con trai Giô-ách, đang đập lấy hạt lúa mì trong một bồn ép nho. Ông làm việc ở đó để người Ma-đi-an không tìm thấy lúa mì.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 와서 아비에셀 사람 요아스에게 속한, 오브라에 [있는] 상수리나무 아래에 앉았다. 그리고 그의 아들 기드온이 미디안에게서 [그것을] 숨기려고 포도주 틀에서 밀을 타작하고 [있었다].
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 오브라에 와서, 아비에셀 사람 요아스의 것인 상수리나무 아래에 앉았다. 요아스의 아들 기드온은 미디안 사람들 눈에 띄지 않게 하려고 포도주 틀에서 밀을 타작하고 있었다.
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 오브라 마을에 왔다. 그는 아비에셀 집안의 요아스에게 속한 큰 나무 아래에 앉았다. 요아스의 아들 기드온은 포도주 틀 안에서 밀 이삭을 두드려 낟알을 털고 있었다. 미디안 사람들이 밀을 찾아내지 못하게 하려고 거기서 그 일을 하고 있었다.

pt.L: E o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio e se sentou debaixo do terebinto que [estava] em Ofra, que [pertencia] a Joás, o abiezrita; e Gideão, seu filho, [estava] malhando trigo no lagar, para [o] esconder de Midiã.
pt.B: Então o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Ofra e se sentou debaixo do terebinto que havia ali, que pertencia a Joás, o abiezrita. Gideão, filho de Joás, estava malhando trigo no lagar, para que os midianitas não o vissem.
pt.R: Então o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio à cidade de Ofra. Ele se sentou ali debaixo de uma árvore grande que pertencia a Joás, da família de Abiezer. Gideão, o filho de Joás, estava batendo o trigo para soltar os grãos, dentro de um lagar. Ele fazia isso ali para que os midianitas não achassem o trigo.

decisions.choice: the angel of Yahweh: God's messenger, in whom God himself is present
decisions.reason: The word means "messenger". In this story the narrator calls the visitor "the angel of Yahweh" (verses 11, 12, 21, 22) and "the angel of God" (verse 20), but also says that "Yahweh turned to him" and "Yahweh said" (verses 14, 16, 23), and Gideon fears he will die because he has seen him face to face (verse 22). The same movement between the messenger and Yahweh himself is found in Genesis 16:7-13, Exodus 3:2-6 and 2:1-4 in this book. The text does not explain how the messenger and Yahweh are related.

decisions.choice: the terebinth: a large, long-lived tree
decisions.reason: The word names a big spreading tree, the terebinth or a kind of oak. Such trees were landmarks and were often places of worship, good or bad (Genesis 35:4; Joshua 24:26; 9:6 in this book).

decisions.choice: beating out wheat in the winepress: threshing in hiding
decisions.reason: Grain was normally threshed on an open threshing floor (verse 37), where the wind carried off the chaff. A winepress was a pit cut into the rock: hidden from view, but cramped. Beating the grain with a stick there, a little at a time, shows how afraid people were of the raiders.

decisions.choice: Joash the Abiezrite: a member of the clan of Abiezer in Manasseh
decisions.reason: Abiezer was a clan of the tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 17:2). Its town Ophrah is a different place from the Ophrah of Benjamin (Joshua 18:23), and its site is not known.

decisions.choice: a big tree; beating the grain out of some wheat
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "terebinth" and for threshing, and adds why Gideon worked inside a winepress.

decisions.choice: "la encina" (L, B), "un árbol grande" (R); "sacudiendo trigo en el lagar"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names a large, long-lived tree, the terebinth (m2). Spanish Bibles have long called such a tree "encina", which a Spanish reader knows; Readable says "un árbol grande", as the English does. Gideon beats the wheat with a stick inside a winepress, a pit cut in rock, rather than on an open threshing floor (m3).

decisions.choice: "Gédéon", and in chapters 6-9 "Joas l'Abiézrite", "Ophra", "Yeroubbaal" (6:32), "Yizréel"
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10: "Gédéon" is the French form used in Hebrews 11:32 and the terms note; "Yeroubbaal" follows the terms note. "Joas" is the usual French form of the name, and "Ophra" and "Abiézer" transcribe the Hebrew as elsewhere in these chapters.

decisions.choice: "cây sồi" (L, B); "một cây lớn" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names a large, long-lived tree (m2), the terebinth, which has no common Vietnamese name; "cây sồi" is the familiar word for such a great tree, and Readable says only "a big tree".

decisions.choice: Gideão, Joás, o abiezrita, Ofra; Abiezer (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the names take their usual Brazilian forms, "Gideão" (not the European "Gedeão"), "Joás", "Ofra", and "o abiezrita" for a man of the clan of Abiezer (m4); Readable says "da família de Abiezer", as the English Readable explains the name.

decisions.choice: o terebinto (L, B), uma árvore grande (R); malhando trigo no lagar (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Terebinto" is the tree m2 names, as Genesis 35:4 has it in Portuguese; Readable says "uma árvore grande", as the English says "a big tree". "Malhar" is the Portuguese verb for beating out grain with a stick, and "lagar" is the winepress, the pit where grapes were trodden (m3).

source.text: וַיֵּרָ֥א אֵלָ֖יו מַלְּאַ֣ךְיְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו יְהוָ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ גִּבּ֥וֹר הֶחָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And appeared to him [the] angel of Yahweh and said to him, Yahweh [is] with you, mighty [man] of strength.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him and said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with you, mighty man of strength."
en.B: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is with you, mighty warrior."
en.R: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed himself to Gideon and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is with you, you strong fighter!"

sw.L: Naye malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtokea, akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [yu] pamoja nawe, ewe shujaa mwenye nguvu."
sw.B: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimtokea, akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja nawe, ewe shujaa hodari."
sw.R: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alijionyesha kwa Gideoni, akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja nawe, wewe mpiganaji hodari!"

es.L: Y se le apareció el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [está] contigo, hombre fuerte y valiente.»
es.B: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se le apareció y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está contigo, guerrero valiente.»
es.R: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se dejó ver por Gedeón y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está contigo, ¡luchador fuerte!»

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui apparut et lui dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] avec toi, vaillant héros. »
fr.B: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} lui apparut et lui dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec toi, vaillant guerrier. »
fr.R: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’est montré à Gédéon et lui a dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec toi, courageux combattant ! »

vi.L: Và thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với ông và nói với ông: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [ở] với ngươi, hỡi người dũng sĩ mạnh mẽ."
vi.B: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với ông và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với con, hỡi chiến sĩ dũng mãnh."
vi.R: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra cho Ghê-đê-ôn thấy và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với con, hỡi người chiến sĩ mạnh mẽ!"

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 그에게 나타나 그에게 말했다. "힘센 용사여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 [계신다]."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 그에게 나타나서 말했다. "용맹한 용사여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 계신다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 기드온에게 모습을 드러내고 말했다. "힘센 용사여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 계신다!"

pt.L: E o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} apareceu a ele e lhe disse: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} [está] contigo, valente guerreiro."
pt.B: O anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} apareceu a ele e disse: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} está contigo, valente guerreiro."
pt.R: O anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se mostrou a Gideão e disse: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} está contigo, valente guerreiro!"

decisions.choice: mighty man of strength: a strong warrior
decisions.reason: The phrase names a brave fighting man (11:1; Joshua 1:14). It can also mean a man of wealth and standing (Ruth 2:1; 1 Samuel 9:1). Spoken to a man hiding in a winepress, it sounds almost like irony, but it also says what Gideon will become with Yahweh's help.

decisions.choice: Yahweh is with you: a statement, not only a greeting
decisions.reason: The words can be a greeting (Ruth 2:4), but Gideon takes them as a claim and questions it (verse 13). Yahweh's promise in verse 16, "I will be with you", picks them up.

decisions.choice: appeared: let himself be seen
decisions.reason: The verb means "was seen". Gideon sees a visitor, but he does not yet know who he is (verse 22).

decisions.choice: showed himself to Gideon
decisions.reason: Readable puts the verb in active form and names Gideon for clarity.

decisions.choice: the angel and the LORD call Gideon "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Genesis note's rule for God speaking to a person: "ngươi" at Literal, "con" at Balanced and Readable where the relationship allows. The angel speaks with the LORD's own voice (m1 at 6:11), so he speaks as God does.

decisions.choice: valente guerreiro (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "valente guerreiro" names a brave fighting man (m1) in two common words, and is short enough to keep its edge as a greeting to a man hiding in a winepress. Readable keeps it, as the sense is plain.

decisions.choice: contigo (tu, the angel to Gideon)
decisions.reason: The angel of the LORD speaks for God, so he addresses Gideon with "tu", as the angels do in Genesis in Portuguese (Genesis 16:9-11), and as the LORD does from verse 14.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֤יו גִּדְעוֹן֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְיֵ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ וְלָ֥מָּה מְצָאַ֖תְנוּ כָּל־זֹ֑את וְאַיֵּ֣ה כָֽל־נִפְלְאֹתָ֡יו אֲשֶׁר֩ סִפְּרוּ־לָ֨נוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֜ינוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲלֹ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ הֶעֱלָ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וְעַתָּה֙ נְטָשָׁ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖נוּ בְּכַף־מִדְיָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Gideon, pardon me, my lord, and if there is Yahweh with us, then why has found us all this? And where [are] all his wonders which recounted to us our fathers, saying, Did not from Egypt bring us up Yahweh? And now has abandoned us Yahweh and given us into [the] palm of Midian.

en.L: And Gideon said to him, "Please, my lord, if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with us, then why has all this found us? And where [are] all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders that our fathers recounted to us, saying, 'Did not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bring us up from Egypt?' But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has abandoned us and given us into the palm of Midian."
en.B: Gideon answered him, "Pardon me, my lord, but if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with us, why has all this come upon us? Where are all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders that our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} told us about when they said, 'Did not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bring us up from Egypt?' Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has abandoned us and handed us over to Midian."
en.R: Gideon said, "Excuse me, sir, but if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with us, why has all this trouble come on us? Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} told us about the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did. They said, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brought us up out of Egypt!' So where are those wonders now? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has left us and let the Midianites take control of us."

sw.L: Naye Gideoni akamwambia, "Tafadhali, bwana wangu, ikiwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja nasi, mbona basi mambo haya yote yametupata? Na yako wapi maajabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote ambayo baba zetu walitusimulia, wakisema, 'Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakutupandisha kutoka Misri?' Lakini sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametuacha, ametutia katika kiganja cha Midiani."
sw.B: Gideoni alimjibu, "Samahani, bwana wangu, lakini ikiwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja nasi, kwa nini mambo haya yote yametupata? Yako wapi maajabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote ambayo mababu zetu walitusimulia, waliposema, 'Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakutupandisha kutoka Misri?' Sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametuacha na kututia mikononi mwa Midiani."
sw.R: Gideoni alisema, "Samahani, bwana, lakini ikiwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja nasi, kwa nini taabu hii yote imetupata? Mababu zetu walitusimulia mambo ya ajabu aliyoyafanya. Walisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitutoa Misri!' Basi yako wapi maajabu hayo sasa? {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametuacha, akawaacha Wamidiani watutawale."

es.L: Y Gedeón le dijo: «Perdón, señor mío, si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está con nosotros, ¿por qué nos ha sobrevenido todo esto? ¿Y dónde [están] todas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} maravillas que nos contaron nuestros padres, diciendo: “¿No nos hizo subir {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de Egipto?” Pero ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos ha abandonado y nos ha entregado en la palma de Madián.»
es.B: Gedeón le respondió: «Perdón, señor mío, pero si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está con nosotros, ¿por qué nos ha pasado todo esto? ¿Dónde están todas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} maravillas que nos contaban nuestros antepasados cuando decían: “¿No nos sacó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de Egipto?” Ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos ha abandonado y nos ha entregado a Madián.»
es.R: Gedeón le dijo: «Perdóname, señor, pero si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está con nosotros, ¿por qué nos han pasado todas estas desgracias? Nuestros antepasados nos contaban las cosas asombrosas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo. Decían: “¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos sacó de Egipto!” Entonces, ¿dónde están ahora esas maravillas? {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos ha dejado y ha permitido que los madianitas nos dominen.»

fr.L: Et Gédéon lui dit : « Pardon, mon seigneur, si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec nous, pourquoi tout cela nous est-il arrivé ? Et où [sont] toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} merveilles que nos pères nous ont racontées, en disant : “N’est-ce pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui nous a fait monter d’Égypte ?” Et maintenant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a abandonnés et nous a livrés dans la paume de Madian. »
fr.B: Gédéon lui répondit : « Pardon, mon seigneur, mais si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec nous, pourquoi tout cela nous est-il arrivé ? Où sont toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} merveilles que nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} nous ont racontées en disant : “N’est-ce pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui nous a fait monter d’Égypte ?” Maintenant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a abandonnés et nous a livrés à Madian. »
fr.R: Gédéon a dit : « Excuse-moi, monsieur, mais si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec nous, pourquoi tous ces malheurs nous sont-ils arrivés ? Nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} nous ont raconté les choses extraordinaires qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faites. Ils disaient : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a fait sortir d’Égypte !” Alors où sont ces merveilles aujourd’hui ? {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} nous a abandonnés et a laissé les Madianites nous dominer. »

vi.L: Và Ghê-đê-ôn nói với người: "Xin lỗi, chúa tôi, nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với chúng tôi, thì sao mọi điều này xảy đến cho chúng tôi? Và đâu [là] mọi việc lạ lùng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà tổ phụ chúng tôi đã thuật lại cho chúng tôi rằng: 'Chẳng phải {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đem chúng ta lên từ Ai Cập sao?' Nhưng bây giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã từ bỏ chúng tôi và phó chúng tôi vào lòng bàn tay Ma-đi-an."
vi.B: Ghê-đê-ôn đáp: "Xin lỗi, chúa tôi, nhưng nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với chúng tôi, sao mọi điều này lại xảy đến cho chúng tôi? Đâu rồi mọi việc lạ lùng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà tổ tiên chúng tôi đã kể cho chúng tôi nghe khi nói: 'Chẳng phải {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đem chúng ta lên từ Ai Cập sao?' Nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã từ bỏ chúng tôi và giao chúng tôi vào tay Ma-đi-an."
vi.R: Ghê-đê-ôn nói: "Xin lỗi ông, nhưng nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với chúng tôi, sao mọi tai họa này lại xảy đến cho chúng tôi? Tổ tiên chúng tôi đã kể cho chúng tôi nghe về những việc lạ lùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm. Họ nói: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đem chúng ta ra khỏi Ai Cập!' Vậy bây giờ những việc lạ lùng ấy ở đâu? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bỏ chúng tôi và để người Ma-đi-an cai trị chúng tôi."

ko.L: 그러자 기드온이 그에게 말했다. "내 주여, 실례지만 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리와 함께 계신다면, 어찌하여 이 모든 일이 우리에게 닥쳤습니까? 우리 조상들이 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리를 이집트에서 올라오게 하지 않으셨느냐?' 하고 우리에게 이야기해 준 그분의 그 모든 놀라운 일들은 어디에 [있습니까]? 그런데 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리를 버리시고, 우리를 미디안의 손바닥에 주셨습니다."
ko.B: 기드온이 그에게 대답했다. "나리, 외람된 말씀이지만, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리와 함께 계신다면 어찌하여 이 모든 일이 우리에게 닥쳤습니까? 우리 조상들이 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리를 이집트에서 이끌어 올리지 않으셨느냐?' 하며 우리에게 들려준 그분의 놀라운 일들은 다 어디에 있습니까? 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 우리를 버리시고 미디안에게 넘기셨습니다."
ko.R: 기드온이 말했다. "나리, 죄송하지만 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리와 함께 계신다면 어째서 이런 고난이 우리에게 닥쳤습니까? 우리 조상들은 주님께서 하신 놀라운 일들을 우리에게 이야기해 주었습니다. 그들은 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리를 이집트에서 이끌어 내셨다!' 하고 말했습니다. 그런데 그런 놀라운 일들이 지금은 어디에 있습니까? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 우리를 버리시고, 미디안 사람들이 우리를 다스리게 하셨습니다."

pt.L: E Gideão lhe disse: "Por favor, meu senhor, se {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} está conosco, então por que nos sobreveio tudo isto? E onde [estão] todas as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} maravilhas que os nossos pais nos contaram, dizendo: 'Não foi do Egito que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} nos fez subir?' Mas agora {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} nos abandonou e nos entregou na palma da mão de Midiã."
pt.B: Gideão lhe respondeu: "Perdoe-me, meu senhor, mas, se {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} está conosco, por que nos aconteceu tudo isto? Onde estão todas as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} maravilhas, de que os nossos {{gender:antepassados|pais}} nos falavam quando diziam: 'Não foi {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} que nos fez subir do Egito?' Agora {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} nos abandonou e nos entregou ao poder de Midiã."
pt.R: Gideão disse: "Desculpe, senhor, mas, se {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} está conosco, por que todo este sofrimento caiu sobre nós? Os nossos {{gender:antepassados|pais}} nos contaram as coisas maravilhosas que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fez. Eles diziam: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} nos tirou do Egito!' Então onde estão essas maravilhas agora? {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} nos abandonou e deixou os midianitas nos dominarem."

decisions.choice: please, my lord: a polite address to a stranger
decisions.reason: The vowels here mark the ordinary "my lord", the courteous way to speak to a superior, not the title used for God (contrast verse 15). Gideon treats the visitor as a man.

decisions.choice: with us: Gideon answers for all Israel
decisions.reason: The visitor said "with you", meaning Gideon alone (verse 12), but Gideon answers "with us". His complaint is about the whole people's suffering.

decisions.choice: wonders: the extraordinary acts of the exodus
decisions.reason: The word is used of the signs and deeds by which Yahweh brought Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:20; 34:10; Psalm 78:11-12).

decisions.choice: Yahweh has abandoned us: Gideon's complaint
decisions.reason: Gideon blames Yahweh for leaving Israel. The prophet has just given the other side: Israel did not listen to Yahweh (verse 10), and 2:12-14 says that Israel abandoned Yahweh first. Yahweh does not argue with Gideon but sends him (verse 14).

decisions.choice: 'The LORD brought us up out of Egypt!'
decisions.reason: The question "Did not the LORD bring us up?" expects the answer yes. Readable gives it as a statement, and moves Gideon's question "where are his wonders" after it.

decisions.choice: sir
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday polite word, since Gideon is speaking to someone he takes for a man.

decisions.choice: "señor mío" (L, B), "señor" (R), in lowercase, with "tú" forms
decisions.reason: Gideon does not yet know who his visitor is, and speaks to him politely as to a stranger (m1). Spanish writes "señor" in lowercase here; in verse 15, where the Hebrew vowels give the title used for God, it becomes "Señor".

decisions.choice: "mon seigneur" in lower case (L, B), "monsieur" (R), with "tu"
decisions.reason: Gideon does not yet know who his visitor is, and speaks to him as to a respected stranger, as the meaning decision says; in verse 15 the Hebrew title changes to the one used for God, and French then writes "mon Seigneur" with a capital, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Gideon calls the visitor "chúa tôi" (L, B), "ông" (R), and himself "tôi"
decisions.reason: He does not yet know who the visitor is, and speaks politely to a stranger (m1), as the Genesis note sets for "my lord" to a man; from verse 15 he speaks to the LORD as "Chúa" and calls himself "con".

decisions.choice: Gideon speaks to the visitor in the formal polite style (합쇼체), calling him "내 주" (L) and "나리" (B, R); the visitor speaks to him in the plain style
decisions.reason: Gideon does not yet know who the visitor is, and *adoni* to a man is "내 주" or "나리", as the terms of this translation set. In verse 15 the Hebrew vowels mark the title for God, and Korean changes to "주님".

decisions.choice: meu senhor, Perdoe-me (B), Desculpe, senhor (R), lowercase
decisions.reason: Gideon takes the visitor for a man (m1), so he speaks as one speaks to a respected stranger, with "meu senhor" and the polite third person ("Perdoe-me", "Desculpe"), as Abraham greets his visitors in Genesis 18:3 in Portuguese. From verse 15, when he knows he is speaking to the LORD, he says "meu Senhor" with a capital and "tu".

source.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֵ֚ךְ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ זֶ֔ה וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ֥ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִכַּ֣ף מִדְיָ֑ן הֲלֹ֖א שְׁלַחְתִּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned to him Yahweh and said, Go in this your strength, and you will deliver Israel from [the] palm of Midian. Have not I sent you?

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you will deliver Israel from the palm of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you will save Israel from Midian's power. Am I not the one sending you?"
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned toward him and said, "Go with the strength you have, and rescue Israel from the Midianites. I am the one who is sending you!"

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamgeukia, akasema, "Nenda kwa nguvu zako hizi, nawe utawaokoa Israeli kutoka kiganjani mwa Midiani. Je, si {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nimekutuma?"
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimgeukia, akasema, "Nenda kwa nguvu hizi ulizo nazo, nawe utawaokoa Israeli kutoka mikononi mwa Midiani. Je, si {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninayekutuma?"
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimgeukia, akasema, "Nenda kwa nguvu ulizo nazo, ukawaokoe Israeli kutoka kwa Wamidiani. Mimi ndiye ninayekutuma!"

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se volvió hacia él y le dijo: «Ve con esta tu fuerza, y librarás a Israel de la palma de Madián. ¿No te he enviado yo?»
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se volvió hacia él y le dijo: «Ve con esta fuerza que tienes, y salvarás a Israel del poder de Madián. ¿No soy yo quien te envía?»
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se volvió hacia él y le dijo: «Ve con la fuerza que tienes, y rescata a Israel de los madianitas. ¡Soy yo quien te envía!»

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se tourna vers lui et dit : « Va avec cette force que tu as, et tu délivreras Israël de la paume de Madian. Ne t’ai-je pas envoyé ? »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se tourna vers lui et dit : « Va avec cette force que tu as, et tu sauveras Israël du pouvoir de Madian. N’est-ce pas moi qui t’envoie ? »
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est tourné vers lui et lui a dit : « Va avec la force que tu as, et délivre Israël des Madianites. C’est moi qui t’envoie ! »

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} quay lại phía ông và phán: "Hãy đi với sức mạnh này của ngươi, và ngươi sẽ giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên khỏi lòng bàn tay Ma-đi-an. Chẳng phải Ta đã sai ngươi sao?"
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} quay lại phía ông và phán: "Hãy đi với sức mạnh con đang có, và con sẽ giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên khỏi tay Ma-đi-an. Chẳng phải chính Ta sai con đi sao?"
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} quay về phía ông và phán: "Hãy đi với sức mạnh con đang có, và giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên khỏi người Ma-đi-an. Chính Ta là Đấng sai con đi!"

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게로 돌아서서 말씀하셨다. "너의 이 힘으로 가거라. 네가 이스라엘을 미디안의 손바닥에서 구원할 것이다. 내가 너를 보내지 않았느냐?"
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그를 바라보며 말씀하셨다. "네가 가진 이 힘으로 가서, 이스라엘을 미디안의 손에서 구하여라. 너를 보내는 이가 내가 아니냐?"
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그를 향하여 말씀하셨다. "네게 있는 힘으로 가서 미디안 사람들에게서 이스라엘을 구하여라. 너를 보내는 이는 바로 나다!"

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} se voltou para ele e disse: "Vai nesta tua força, e salvarás Israel da palma da mão de Midiã. Não te enviei eu?"
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} se voltou para ele e disse: "Vai com essa força que tens, e livrarás Israel do poder de Midiã. Não sou eu quem te envia?"
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} se voltou para Gideão e disse: "Vai com a força que tens e livra Israel dos midianitas. Sou eu quem está te enviando!"

decisions.choice: Yahweh turned to him: the visitor now speaks as Yahweh
decisions.reason: The narrator no longer says "the angel of Yahweh" but "Yahweh", and the visitor speaks with Yahweh's own authority: "Have I not sent you?" See verse 11.

decisions.choice: this strength of yours: the strength you have now
alternatives: the strength I have just spoken of
decisions.reason: "This" may point to Gideon's strength as it is, weak as he thinks it (verse 15), or to the strength promised in verse 12, "Yahweh is with you". Either way Gideon is to go as he is, without waiting to become stronger.

decisions.choice: deliver: rescue from an enemy
decisions.reason: This is the work of the judges whom Yahweh raised up (2:16, 18; 3:9, 31).

decisions.choice: Have I not sent you?: a firm statement
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. It is Yahweh's commission, like the sending of Moses (Exodus 3:10-12).

decisions.choice: pronouns for the visitor follow the narrator's name for him
decisions.reason: Where the narrator calls the speaker "the LORD" (verses 14-18, 23), English marks the pronouns for him as pronouns for God; where he is called "the angel", it does not.

decisions.choice: I am the one who is sending you!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָ֔י בַּמָּ֥ה אוֹשִׁ֖יעַ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנֵּ֤ה אַלְפִּי֙ הַדַּ֣ל בִּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וְאָנֹכִ֥י הַצָּעִ֖יר בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, pardon me, my Lord, by what will I deliver Israel? Look, my clan [is] the weak[est] in Manasseh, and I [am] the least in [the] house of my father.

en.L: And he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Please, my Lord, how will I deliver Israel? Look, my clan [is] the weakest in Manasseh, and I [am] the least in my father's house."
en.B: Gideon said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Pardon me, my Lord, but how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my family."
en.R: Gideon said, "Please, Lord, how could I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in the tribe of Manasseh. And in my family I am the least important."

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Tafadhali, Bwana wangu, nitawaokoaje Israeli? Tazama, ukoo wangu [ndio] dhaifu kuliko yote katika Manase, nami [ni] mdogo kuliko wote katika nyumba ya baba yangu."
sw.B: Gideoni akamwambia, "Samahani, Bwana wangu, lakini nitawezaje kuwaokoa Israeli? Ukoo wangu ndio dhaifu kuliko yote katika Manase, nami ni mdogo kuliko wote katika jamaa yangu."
sw.R: Gideoni alisema, "Tafadhali, Bwana, ningewezaje kuwaokoa Israeli? Ukoo wangu ndio dhaifu kuliko yote katika kabila la Manase. Na katika jamaa yangu mimi ndiye mdogo kuliko wote."

es.L: Y él {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Perdón, Señor mío, ¿con qué libraré a Israel? Mira, mi clan [es] el más débil de Manasés, y yo [soy] el menor en la casa de mi padre.»
es.B: Gedeón {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Perdón, Señor mío, pero ¿cómo podré salvar a Israel? Mi clan es el más débil de Manasés, y yo soy el menor de mi familia.»
es.R: Gedeón dijo: «Por favor, Señor, ¿cómo podría yo rescatar a Israel? Mi clan es el más débil de la tribu de Manasés. Y en mi familia yo soy el menos importante.»

fr.L: Et il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Pardon, mon Seigneur, avec quoi délivrerai-je Israël ? Voici, mon clan [est] le plus faible en Manassé, et moi, je [suis] le plus petit dans la maison de mon père. »
fr.B: Gédéon {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Pardon, mon Seigneur, mais comment pourrais-je sauver Israël ? Mon clan est le plus faible de Manassé, et je suis le plus petit de ma famille. »
fr.R: Gédéon a dit : « S’il te plaît, Seigneur, comment est-ce que je pourrais délivrer Israël ? Mon clan est le plus faible de la tribu de Manassé. Et dans ma famille, c’est moi le moins important. »

vi.L: Và ông thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, con lấy gì mà giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên? Kìa, gia tộc con [là] yếu nhất trong Ma-na-se, và con [là] nhỏ nhất trong nhà cha con."
vi.B: Ghê-đê-ôn thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, xin thứ lỗi, nhưng làm sao con giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên được? Gia tộc con yếu nhất trong Ma-na-se, và con là người nhỏ nhất trong gia đình."
vi.R: Ghê-đê-ôn thưa: "Lạy Chúa, làm sao con có thể giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên được? Gia tộc con yếu nhất trong chi tộc Ma-na-se. Còn trong gia đình, con là người kém quan trọng nhất."

ko.L: 그러자 그가 그분께 말했다. "주님, 제가 무엇으로 이스라엘을 구원하겠습니까? 보십시오, 제 집안은 므낫세에서 가장 약하고, 저는 제 아버지의 집에서 가장 작은 사람입니다."
ko.B: 기드온이 그분께 말했다. "주님, 송구하지만 제가 어떻게 이스라엘을 구할 수 있겠습니까? 제 집안은 므낫세 지파에서 가장 약하고, 저는 제 가족 가운데서 가장 보잘것없는 사람입니다."
ko.R: 기드온이 말했다. "주님, 제가 어떻게 이스라엘을 구할 수 있겠습니까? 제 집안은 므낫세 지파에서 가장 약한 집안입니다. 그리고 저는 우리 가족 가운데서 가장 보잘것없는 사람입니다."

pt.L: E ele {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Ah, meu Senhor, com que salvarei Israel? Eis que o meu clã [é] o mais fraco em Manassés, e eu [sou] o menor na casa do meu pai."
pt.B: Gideão {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} respondeu: "Perdoa-me, meu Senhor, mas como posso livrar Israel? O meu clã é o mais fraco de Manassés, e eu sou o menor da minha família."
pt.R: Gideão disse: "Por favor, Senhor, como eu poderia livrar Israel? O meu clã é o mais fraco da tribo de Manassés. E na minha família eu sou o menos importante."

decisions.choice: my Lord: the vowels mark the title used for God
decisions.reason: The consonants are the same as "my lord" in verse 13, but here the scribes pointed the word as the title reserved for God. They read Gideon as now speaking to Yahweh, who has just spoken to him (verse 14). Gideon himself may still be speaking politely to a stranger, since he only realizes who the visitor is in verse 22.

decisions.choice: my clan: the word often means "thousand"
decisions.reason: The word usually means "a thousand", but it can name a clan or a fighting unit raised from a clan (1 Samuel 10:19; see Numbers 1). Here it is Gideon's clan, Abiezer.

decisions.choice: the least: the youngest or the smallest in standing
decisions.reason: The word can mean "youngest" or "most insignificant". Either way Gideon says he is the last person anyone would choose. Yahweh often chooses the least likely (1 Samuel 9:21; 16:11).

decisions.choice: my family
decisions.reason: "My father's house" means the extended family Gideon belongs to.

decisions.choice: "Bwana wangu" with a capital here, against "bwana wangu" in verse 13
decisions.reason: In verse 13 Gideon speaks to a stranger with the ordinary polite "my lord"; here the Hebrew vowels mark the title used for God. Swahili uses one word for both, so the capital B carries the difference, as the English capital L does.

decisions.choice: "주님" for *Adonai* here, where verse 13 had "내 주" / "나리"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels mark the title used for God (m1), so Korean uses the word it keeps for God, as the terms of this translation set for *Adonai*.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa", and "con" for himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels here mark the title used for God (m1), so Gideon now speaks as one praying: "Chúa" for the Lord and "con" for himself, as the Genesis note sets.

decisions.choice: meu Senhor, Perdoa-me (tu), from here on
decisions.reason: The scribes pointed the word here as the title for God (m1), and the English marks the pronouns for the speaker as God's from verse 14 (r-en-1 there). Portuguese shows the change in two ways: "Senhor" takes a capital, and Gideon now addresses him with "tu" ("Perdoa-me", "teus olhos" in verse 17), as people speak to God, where in verse 13 he said "Perdoe-me, meu senhor".

decisions.choice: I will be with you: the promise made to Moses
decisions.reason: Yahweh used the same words when he sent Moses to Pharaoh and Moses protested that he was unfit (Exodus 3:11-12). Gideon's weakness is answered with Yahweh's presence, not with a reason to trust himself.

decisions.choice: as one man: all at once, as easily as one man
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that the enemy will fall together, in one blow (Numbers 14:15), or that defeating them will be as easy as defeating a single man. Both point to a complete victory.

decisions.choice: as easily as if you were fighting just one man
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture; see m2.

decisions.choice: if I have found favor in your eyes: a polite request
decisions.reason: The phrase is a courteous way to ask a favor of someone greater (Genesis 18:3; Exodus 33:13).

decisions.choice: sign: proof
decisions.reason: Gideon asks for something that will show the promise is real, as Moses was given signs (Exodus 3:12; 4:1-9). The sign comes in verse 21.

decisions.choice: that you are speaking with me: that it is really you
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is stressed. Gideon wants to know who is speaking: whether this visitor truly speaks for Yahweh.

decisions.choice: the quotation runs on into verse 18
decisions.reason: Gideon's words continue in the next verse, so the closing quotation mark comes there.

decisions.choice: "dấu hiệu" for the sign
decisions.reason: A sign that proves who is speaking (m2); "dấu lạ" is kept for the signs of John, which are miracles, and "dấu hiệu" is the plain proof Gideon asks for here and in verses 36-40.

decisions.choice: "표징" for the sign Gideon asks for
alternatives: "표적", the word for Jesus's signs in John
decisions.reason: "표징" is a plain word for a token or proof; "표적" is kept for the miraculous signs of the Gospels. Gideon speaks to God in the formal polite style with "주님" and "저", as in prayer.

decisions.choice: my offering: a gift, which could be a meal or a sacrifice
decisions.reason: The word means a gift brought to honor someone, and it is also the word for the grain offering in worship (Leviticus 2:1). Gideon may be preparing a meal for an honored guest, as Abraham did (Genesis 18:1-8), or an offering; the visitor turns it into an offering by fire (verse 21).

decisions.choice: I, I will stay: I myself will wait
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stressed: the visitor himself promises to wait for Gideon.

decisions.choice: a gift of food
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gift turns out to be (verse 19).

decisions.choice: come back
decisions.reason: Gideon will leave and "come" to the visitor again; Balanced and Readable say "come back".

decisions.choice: deity pronoun setting on "toi", "tes", "t'" and "lui" where Gideon speaks to the visitor or of him, from verse 15, as on the English "you", "your" and "him"; not on "te" in the polite formula "je te prie" and "s'il te plaît"
alternatives: a setting on every pronoun for the visitor
decisions.reason: As in the English, the visitor is spoken of with the deity pronoun setting once the narrator calls him "the LORD" (verse 14). In the fixed polite formulas "je te prie" and "s'il te plaît", the pronoun is part of the phrase, and the English "please" has none, so French adds no setting there.
